u0285.gist: The Supreme Court held that Section 498A IPC protection against cruelty can extend to women in live-in relationships 'in the nature of marriage'.
facts: Case: Dr. Lokesh B.H. & Others v. State of Karnataka & Another; decided 3 August 2026.
Two conditions: relationship in the nature of marriage, and a genuine intention to marry.
The woman bears the initial burden of proving both conditions.
Section 498A IPC punished cruelty by husband or his relatives: up to three years and fine.
Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the matching offence is Section 85.
Indra Sarma v. V.K.V. Sarma (2013): live-in between consenting adults is not an offence.

mcq.q: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita corresponds to Section 498A IPC (cruelty), discussed by the Supreme Court in August 2026?
mcq.why: The corresponding offence of Section 498A IPC is Section 85 of the BNS.

u0286.gist: The Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan, the National Offshore Exploration Scheme, to speed up oil and gas exploration in deepwater and frontier offshore basins.
facts: Approved on July 31, 2026; Phase-I outlay ₹84,084 crore up to FY 2030–31.
Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
Vision announced by PM Modi from the Red Fort on Independence Day 2025.
Aims to add more than 600 MMTOE (Million Metric Tonnes of Oil Equivalent) of hydrocarbon reserves.
₹43,200 crore for 60 wells; government covers up to 50%, capped at ₹675 crore per well.
Other parts: data acquisition ₹28,534 crore; common infrastructure hubs ₹10,000 crore; manufacturing zone ₹2,000 crore.
u0286.hook: Samudra Manthan = churning of the ocean; here India 'churns' the sea-bed for oil and gas.
u0286.check: The four listed components add up to ₹83,734 crore, not the stated ₹84,084 crore.

mcq.q: What is the Phase-I outlay of 'Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme' approved by the Cabinet in July 2026?
mcq.why: The Cabinet approved a Phase-I outlay of ₹84,084 crore up to FY 2030–31.

u0287.gist: DoT and the Madhya Pradesh government signed an MoU on 30 July 2026 to set up India's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone at Gwalior.
facts: Planned as a 350-acre plug-and-play industrial cluster; bhumi pujan due on October 29, 2026.
Centre approved ₹493 crore for Phase-I core infrastructure.
SPV equity: Madhya Pradesh government 51%, Department of Telecommunications 49%.
Will cover mobile phones, telecom equipment, optical fibre, semiconductors, components and 5G-6G technologies.
Investment expected to cross ₹10,000 crore in the second phase.
Mobile-phone production rose from ₹18,000 crore to ₹6.2 lakh crore (FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26).
u0287.check: The last paragraph, on the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act 1971, is unrelated to the Telecom Manufacturing Zone.

mcq.q: India's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone, for which an MoU was signed in July 2026, will be set up in which city?
mcq.why: DoT and Madhya Pradesh signed an MoU to set up India's first TMZ at Gwalior.

u0288.gist: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026 sharply raises penalties for exam cheating and sets fast-track trials.
facts: Introduced by Dr. Jitendra Singh (27 July); passed both Houses by 30 July; assent 31 July 2026.
Amends the 2024 Act; covers UPSC, SSC, Railway Recruitment Boards, IBPS, NTA and central ministries.
Individuals: jail raised from 3–5 to 5–10 years; maximum fine ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh.
Service providers: fine up to ₹5 crore (from ₹1 crore); debarment up to eight years (from four).
Organised crime: 7–10 years' jail and a minimum ₹10 crore fine.
Investigation within two months; Special Fast Track Courts to finish trials within three months of charge sheet.
u0288.trap: Individual's maximum fine ₹50 lakh; service provider's maximum ₹5 crore; organised crime minimum ₹10 crore.

mcq.q: Under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026, what is the jail term for individuals using unfair means?
mcq.why: For individuals, imprisonment increases from 3–5 years to 5–10 years.

u0289.gist: The Education Ministry released PGI 2.0 for 2025–26 on 7 July 2026; only Chandigarh reached Uttam-3, and no State/UT reached the top three grades.
facts: PGI-S covers all 36 States/UTs; PGI-D covers 784 districts.
PGI introduced 2017; first report 2019 (for 2017-18); PGI-S: 70 indicators, maximum 1,000 points.
Highest: Chandigarh (766.0), the only Uttam-3 (761-820); lowest: Meghalaya (525.7); gap 240.3.
Inter-State performance gap fell from 51% (2017-18) to 31.4% (2025-26).
No State/UT in the top grades Utkarsh (941-1000), Uttam-1 or Uttam-2.
Prachesta-1 (701-760): DNH&DD, Punjab, Kerala, Delhi; Uttar Pradesh among 13 in Akanshi-1 (521-580).
u0289.hook: Grade ladder, top to bottom: Utkarsh → Uttam → Prachesta → Akanshi.
u0289.trap: PGI started in 2017, but the first report came in 2019 (reference year 2017-18).

mcq.q: In the Performance Grading Index 2.0 (2025–26) for States/UTs, which was the only State/UT to attain the Uttam-3 grade?
mcq.why: Only Chandigarh fell in the Uttam-3 band (761-820), with the top score of 766.0.

mcq.q: In the Performance Grading Index 2.0 (2025–26), which State/UT recorded the lowest score?
mcq.why: Meghalaya recorded the lowest score, 525.7; Chandigarh the highest, 766.0.

u0290.gist: The Education Ministry released AISHE reports on 8 July 2026; India's higher education GER rose to 30.0 in 2023–24, with female GER above male.
facts: AISHE 2023–24 is the 14th edition; 64,756 institutions incl. 1,289 universities and 48,246 colleges.
Total enrolment about 4.5 crore (3.4 crore in 2014–15); women 49.7%; 76.8% at undergraduate level.
GER 30.0 (29.5 in 2022–23); male 28.9, female 31.2; Gender Parity Index 1.08.
Uttar Pradesh is first in the list of seven States with highest student enrolment.
58,134 foreign students from 173 countries; Nepal has the largest share.
18 women-only universities and 19 open universities; about 17.3 lakh teachers; Pupil-Teacher Ratio 23.
u0290.trap: Female GER (31.2) is higher than male GER (28.9), so GPI is above one (1.08).

mcq.q: According to AISHE 2023–24, released in July 2026, what was India's Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education?
mcq.why: India's higher education GER increased to 30.0 in 2023–24 from 29.5 in 2022–23.

mcq.q: As per AISHE 2023–24, which country accounts for the highest share of foreign students in India?
mcq.why: Of 58,134 foreign students from 173 countries, Nepal had the highest share.

u0291.gist: The UDISE+ Report 2025–26, released on 7 July 2026, shows more teachers, lower dropout and better school facilities such as computers and internet.
facts: Dropout fell: preparatory 2.3% to 1.8%; secondary 8.2% to 7.0% (2024–25 to 2025–26).
Secondary GER rose from 68.5% to 71.7%; secondary retention 47.2% to 51.9%.
Single-teacher schools fell to 1,00,843; zero-enrolment schools fell from 7,993 to 5,663.
Schools with computers 69.9% and internet 67.4% in 2025–26.
Girls are 48.4% of enrolment; female teachers 54.9% (2025–26).
u0291.hook: UDISE+ = Unified District Information System for Education Plus.
u0291.trap: Middle-level GER fell slightly (90.3% to 89.6%) even as secondary GER rose.

mcq.q: According to the UDISE+ Report 2025–26, what was the secondary-level dropout rate in 2025–26?
mcq.why: The secondary-level dropout rate declined from 8.2% to 7.0%.

u0292.gist: On 15 July 2026, the Cabinet approved two elevated highway corridors in Varanasi and the National Investment Policy for Urea-2026.
facts: Two Varanasi corridors cost about ₹25,446 crore; built by NHAI under the Hybrid Annuity Model.
Part of the Varanasi Decongestion Plan; aligned with PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan.
43.218-km Varuna River corridor: NH-31 to Varanasi Ring Road, ₹10,998.32 crore.
46.039-km Ganga River corridor: NH-19 to Varanasi Ring Road, ₹14,447.64 crore.
NIPU-2026 updates the New Investment Policy, 2012, to achieve urea self-reliance.
Plans eight to nine new gas-based plants adding about 10 million tonnes yearly; returns on equity 12%–16%.
u0292.trap: Varuna corridor: 43.218 km, NH-31; Ganga corridor: 46.039 km, NH-19 – don't swap.

mcq.q: The 46.039-km elevated corridor approved for Varanasi in July 2026 runs along which river?
mcq.why: The 46.039-km corridor along the Ganga will connect NH-19 to Varanasi Ring Road.

u0293.gist: Delhi notified EV Policy 2.0 for 1 July 2026–31 March 2030, moving new registrations of three- and two-wheelers to electric only.
facts: Cabinet approved it on June 29, 2026; CM Rekha Gupta defended the petrol two-wheeler cut-off.
From 1 January 2027: only electric three-wheelers and N1-category trucks will be registered.
From 1 April 2028: only electric two-wheelers registered; existing vehicles may complete their life.
School buses: at least 10% electric within two years; 30% by 31 March 2030.
Direct investment over ₹7,000 crore; overall plan ₹15,000 crore.
Target 32,000 public charging points (about 9,000 working); ₹1,000 crore for charging.
u0293.trap: Three-wheelers and N1 trucks go electric-only from 1 January 2027; two-wheelers from 1 April 2028.

mcq.q: Under Delhi EV Policy 2.0, from which date will only electric two-wheelers be registered in Delhi?
mcq.why: From 1 April 2028, only electric two-wheelers will be registered in Delhi.

u0294.gist: The Department of Health Research released a draft National Health Research Policy 2026, updating the 2011 policy and proposing much higher public research spending.
facts: DHR is under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; public comments invited until July 27, 2026.
Public health-research spending: about 0.024% of GDP in 2026–27.
Target: 0.072% by 2037 and 0.15% by 2047 – over six times today's level.
Even then it stays below the 0.27% weighted average of high-income countries.
Proposes a National Health Research Agenda and a National Health Research Stewardship Committee.
u0294.hook: 0.024 → 0.072 (2037) → 0.15 (2047): triple first, then over six times.

mcq.q: The draft National Health Research Policy 2026 proposes raising public health-research spending to what share of GDP by 2047?
mcq.why: It proposes 0.072% by 2037 and 0.15% by 2047, from about 0.024% now.

u0295.gist: A TRG Datacenters study ranked India ninth among nearly 100 countries least vulnerable to a major internet blackout; the United States ranked first.
facts: India's digital vulnerability score: 23.4; it is among the ten best-prepared countries.
India has 22 submarine internet cables and 40 Internet Exchange Points.
About 70% of India's population uses the internet.
USA best prepared (score zero), then Indonesia (10.3) and United Kingdom (16.2).
TRG Datacenters is a US-based digital infrastructure provider, acquired by Tallvine Partners.

mcq.q: In a TRG Datacenters study on internet blackout preparedness, at which position was India ranked globally?
mcq.why: India ranked ninth with a digital vulnerability score of 23.4.

u0296.gist: NITI Aayog's roadmap aims to turn Ayurveda into a regulated, evidence-based global healthcare system, integrated into national health systems by 2047.
facts: Prepared by NITI Aayog's Health Division with PricewaterhouseCoopers under its Research Scheme.
Linked to Viksit Bharat @2047 and 'One Earth, One Health'.
India has about 3,55,000 trained Ayurveda practitioners; research spans nearly 70 countries.
WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre is in Jamnagar, Gujarat; ICD-11 includes Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani.
Proposed Global Ayurveda Register under the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine.
Ayush and herbal exports: USD 1.09 billion (2014) to USD 2.16 billion (2023).
u0296.hook: Ayush exports roughly doubled: 1.09 → 2.16 billion USD.

mcq.q: Where is the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre, mentioned in NITI Aayog's Ayurveda roadmap, located?
mcq.why: The WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre is in Jamnagar, Gujarat.

u0297.gist: Ken-Betwa project-affected tribal families and farmers renewed protests on 3 July 2026 near Chhatarpur, saying promises made in April were unfulfilled.
facts: Protest by the Barana River near Kupi village, Chhatarpur; included Jal, Faansi and Mitti Satyagrahas.
MP Cabinet raised the package by about ₹202.50 crore; compensation ₹5 lakh to ₹12.5 lakh per family.
Project launched by PM Modi on 25 December 2024; first of 30 river-linking projects (National Perspective Plan).
Moves surplus Ken water to the Betwa basin; helps Bundelkhand in MP and UP; both are Yamuna tributaries.
Phase I: 77-metre Daudhan Dam, two powerhouses, 216.46-km link canal with a 2-km tunnel.
Canal will irrigate 1,93,899 hectares en route; 50.93 MCM reaches Betwa for Lalitpur.
u0297.hook: Ken (surplus) → Betwa (deficit); both rivers end up in the Yamuna.
u0297.trap: Phase I = Daudhan Dam and link canal; Phase II = Lower Orr Dam, Kotha Barrage and Bina Complex.

mcq.q: Phase I of the Ken-Betwa Link Project, whose affected families protested in July 2026, proposes which 77-metre-high dam?
mcq.why: Phase I proposes the 77-metre-high Daudhan Dam and a 216.46-km link canal.

u0298.gist: PM Modi inaugurated Noida International Airport (Phase-1) at Jewar on 28 March 2026; commercial flights began on 15 June 2026.
facts: DGCA aerodrome licence: March 6, 2026; first commercial flight: IndiGo, arriving from Lucknow.
Located in Jewar, Gautam Buddha Nagar district; built at ₹11,200 crore.
Cargo terminal opened; foundation stone laid for an MRO (Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul) facility.
Uttar Pradesh now has five international airports, among the highest in India.
Developer: Yamuna International Airport Private Limited, a 100% subsidiary of Zurich Airport International AG (PPP).
Project approved in 2003 under PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee; Akasa Air to set up its first MRO here.
u0298.trap: Licence 6 March, inauguration 28 March, commercial operations 15 June 2026 – three different dates.

mcq.q: Which company is developing Noida International Airport at Jewar, inaugurated in March 2026?
mcq.why: YIAPL, a 100% subsidiary of Zurich Airport International AG, develops and operates it.

mcq.q: Which airline operated the first commercial flight to Noida International Airport on 15 June 2026?
mcq.why: The first commercial flight, operated by IndiGo, arrived from Lucknow.

u0299.gist: NCRB's ADSI 2024 report (released 6 May 2026) shows accidental deaths rose to 4,67,857 while suicides fell slightly to 1,70,746.
facts: Age group 30–45 years had the most accidental deaths: 1,46,370 (31.3%).
Forces of nature: 7,903 deaths; lightning 35.7%, heat/sunstroke 23.2%.
Maharashtra had the largest share of accidental deaths (16.2%); Uttar Pradesh 9.2%.
Road accidents caused 1,75,142 deaths (87.8% of traffic-accident deaths); 59.7% of road accidents were rural.
Suicide rate 12.2 per lakh; family problems 33.5% and illness 18.0% of suicides.
u0299.trap: Total accidental deaths (4,67,857) and number of road accidents (4,67,967) look alike but are different figures.

mcq.q: According to NCRB's ADSI 2024 report, which state had the highest share of accidental deaths in 2024?
mcq.why: Maharashtra had 16.2%, ahead of Madhya Pradesh (9.8%) and Uttar Pradesh (9.2%).

mcq.q: As per ADSI 2024, what share of accidental deaths due to forces of nature was caused by lightning?
mcq.why: Of 7,903 deaths due to forces of nature, 35.7% were due to lightning.

u0300.gist: The Election Commission announced Phase III of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls on 14 May 2026, covering 16 States and 3 Union Territories.
facts: Began on May 30, 2026; about 3.94 lakh Booth Level Officers cover 36.73 crore electors.
Not covered in Phase III: Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.
Legal basis: Articles 324 and 326; Sections 16, 19, 21 and 22 of RP Act, 1950.
SC (ADR v. ECI, 27 May 2026) held SIR is within ECI's statutory mandate.
Phase I: Bihar (June–September 2025); electors 7.89 crore to about 7.42 crore.
Phase II: nine States incl. UP and three UTs; about 50.99 crore to 45.81 crore (−10.2%).
u0300.trap: Phase III = 16 States + 3 UTs; the first two phases together covered 13 States/UTs.
u0300.check: Text says Odisha, Mizoram, Sikkim and Manipur publish final rolls on 6 September, but the table gives Odisha 21 September and Mizoram 7 September.

mcq.q: Which of the following was NOT covered in Phase III of the Special Intensive Revision announced in May 2026?
mcq.why: Phase III will not cover Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.

u0301.gist: 2026 Assembly polls in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Assam and Puducherry brought BJP to power in Bengal and TVK in Tamil Nadu.
facts: Schedule announced March 15, 2026; polling in April; counting on May 4, 2026.
West Bengal: BJP won 208 of 294; Suvendu Adhikari first BJP CM (May 9, 2026); TMC 80.
Tamil Nadu: TVK won 108 of 234; C. Joseph Vijay CM (May 10); first non-DMK/AIADMK CM since 1967.
Kerala: UDF won 102 of 140; V.D. Satheesan (INC) sworn in May 18, 2026.
Assam: BJP 82 of 126; Himanta Biswa Sarma's second consecutive term (May 12, 2026).
Puducherry: NDA 18 of 30 (AINRC 12); N. Rangasamy sworn in May 13, 2026.
u0301.hook: House sizes: West Bengal 294, Tamil Nadu 234, Kerala 140, Assam 126, Puducherry 30.
u0301.trap: TVK won 108 seats, but Vijay had support of 120 MLAs-elect with allies.
u0301.check: West Bengal 'combined provisional' turnout (93.7%) is higher than both phase figures (93.19%, 91.66%), which is not possible. Kerala Governor's name is misspelt 'Rajednra'.

mcq.q: Who became the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal after the 2026 Assembly elections?
mcq.why: Suvendu Adhikari took oath as the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal on May 9, 2026.

mcq.q: In the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly election, how many seats did Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) win?
mcq.why: TVK won 108 of 234 seats; Vijay had support of 120 MLAs-elect.

u0302.gist: NCRB's Crime in India 2024 report (6 May 2026) shows total crime fell about 6%, but cybercrime rose 17.9% to 1,01,928 cases.
facts: Total cases: 58,85,867 in 2024, down from 62.41 lakh in 2023; crime rate 448.3 to 418.9.
Cybercrime: 1,01,928 cases (+17.9%); financial fraud 73,987 cases (72.6%).
Crimes against women fell 1.5% to 4.41 lakh; Uttar Pradesh highest with 66,398 cases.
'Cruelty by husband or his relatives' formed 27.2% (1,20,227 cases) of crimes against women.
UP also highest in crimes against SCs (14,642) and dowry deaths (2,057 victims); MP highest against STs (3,165).
Drug overdose deaths up 50% to 978 (Tamil Nadu highest, 313); Kerala top charge-sheeting (94.5%).
u0302.trap: '4.41 lakh' appears twice: crimes against women (2024) and hurt-category cases (2024).

mcq.q: According to NCRB's Crime in India 2024 report, which state recorded the highest number of crimes against women?
mcq.why: Uttar Pradesh reported the highest crimes against women, with 66,398 cases.

mcq.q: As per Crime in India 2024, what share of cybercrime cases related to financial fraud?
mcq.why: 73,987 of 1,01,928 cybercrime cases, or 72.6%, were financial fraud.

u0303.gist: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026 makes disrupting the singing of 'Vande Mataram' a crime, like the National Anthem.
facts: President Droupadi Murmu gave assent on August 11, 2026.
Cabinet approved on May 5, 2026; Lok Sabha passed it on July 30, 2026 (Rajya Sabha earlier).
Amends the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.
Section 3 penalty: jail up to three years, or fine, or both – now also for Vande Mataram.
Vande Mataram by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee: first in Bangadarshan (1875), later in Anandamath (1882).
Set to music by Rabindranath Tagore, who sang it at the 1896 INC session.
u0303.hook: Bankim's song timeline: '75 Bangadarshan → '82 Anandamath → '96 Tagore sings at INC.
u0303.trap: Rajya Sabha cleared the Bill before the Lok Sabha passed it (30 July 2026).

mcq.q: 'Vande Mataram', given legal protection by a 2026 amendment, was first published in 1875 in which publication?
mcq.why: It was first published in Bangadarshan (1875) and later included in Anandamath (1882).

u0304.gist: The Panchayati Raj Ministry released Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0 for FY 2023–24 on National Panchayati Raj Day, 24 April 2026.
facts: PAI measures Gram Panchayat performance; it was earlier called Panchayat Development Index (PDI).
Nine themes, from poverty-free livelihoods to women-friendly Panchayat; PAI 2.0 portal launched May 26, 2025.
33 of 36 States/UTs took part; West Bengal was the only State left out.
2,59,867 Panchayats gave validated data (97.30% of 2,66,999).
No Panchayat reached A+ (Achiever, 90+); 3,635 were A-grade, Tripura the most (943).
Uttar Pradesh had the most B-grade/Performer (18,905) and most D-grade/Beginner (6,124) Panchayats.
u0304.hook: Grades: A+ Achiever, A Front Runner, B Performer, C Aspirant, D Beginner.
u0304.trap: Tripura leads A-grade; Uttar Pradesh leads both B-grade and D-grade counts.

mcq.q: Which state did not participate in the Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0 (FY 2023–24) released in April 2026?
mcq.why: 27 of 28 States took part; West Bengal was the only non-participating State.

mcq.q: In the Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0 (FY 2023–24), which state had the highest number of B-grade (Performer) Panchayats?
mcq.why: Uttar Pradesh had 18,905 B-grade Panchayats, ahead of Gujarat with 11,963.

u0305.gist: The Health Ministry launched JANANI, a digital platform tracking care of mothers and newborns, upgrading the old Reproductive and Child Health portal.
facts: JANANI = Journey of Antenatal, Natal and Neonatal Integrated Care.
Launched at the National Summit on Innovation and Inclusivity.
Builds a longitudinal (over-time) health record: antenatal, delivery, postnatal, newborn care, family planning.
Key feature: QR-enabled digital Mother and Child Health (MCH) cards.
Can integrate with U-WIN and POSHAN platforms.
So far: 1.34 crore registrations, over 30 lakh pregnant women, over 30 lakh digital MCH cards.
u0305.hook: JANANI (जननी = mother): a platform for mothers and newborns.

mcq.q: JANANI, launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2026, is an upgraded version of which existing portal?
mcq.why: JANANI is an upgraded version of the existing Reproductive and Child Health portal.

u0306.gist: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, to enlarge the Lok Sabha and restart delimitation, failed in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026.
facts: Introduced 16 April 2026; got 298 votes for and 230 against.
With 528 present and voting, 352 votes were needed (special majority).
Proposed raising maximum Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850 (815 from States, 35 from UTs).
Amendments proposed to Articles 81, 82 and 170, and a new definition of 'population'.
'Population' would mean the census chosen by Parliament by law; Delimitation Commission to redraw seats.
Aims included earlier implementation of one-third reservation for women.
u0306.trap: More yes than no votes (298 vs 230), yet the Bill failed because 352 votes were required.

mcq.q: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposed raising the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to what?
mcq.why: An amendment to Article 81 proposed raising maximum Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850.

mcq.q: How many votes were required for the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 to pass in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026?
mcq.why: With 528 members present and voting, 352 votes were required; it got only 298.

u0307.gist: MoEFCC notified the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026 on 31 March 2026, refining definitions and making recycled-content labels mandatory.
facts: They amend, not replace, the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016.
End-of-Life Disposal now includes co-processing, waste-to-energy, waste-to-oil and road construction.
Turning plastic into feedstock or new plastic counts strictly as recycling, not disposal.
Plastic Waste Processors now include recyclers and end-of-life disposal entities.
New terms: Registered Environment Auditor, Reuse and Seller.
Recycled plastic packaging must meet IS 14534:2023 and carry recycled-content labels.
u0307.trap: Feedstock or new plastic = recycling; energy recovery (waste-to-energy, road building) = end-of-life disposal.

mcq.q: Under the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026, recycled plastic packaging must comply with which Indian Standard?
mcq.why: All recycled plastic packaging must comply with Indian Standard IS 14534:2023.

u0308.gist: MHA released PRAHAAR, India's first national counter-terrorism policy and strategy, on 23 February 2026, for a uniform, technology-aware response to terror.
facts: Strategy was announced in November 2024; came after the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.
Covers terrorism, terror financing, radicalisation, cyberattacks, drone threats and attacks on critical infrastructure.
Threats seen across land, air and water, plus the cyber domain.
Names Al-Qaeda and ISIS as using sleeper cells and propaganda; notes cross-border sponsored terrorism.
Flags drones, encrypted apps, dark web and crypto wallets used by terror groups.
CBRNED = Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, Explosive and Digital materials.

mcq.q: What is the name of India's first national counter-terrorism policy and strategy released by MHA in February 2026?
mcq.why: MHA released India's first national counter-terrorism policy, PRAHAAR, on 23 February 2026.

u0309.gist: Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh announced plans on 6 March 2026 to restrict children's social media use, as Australia already bars under-16 accounts.
facts: Karnataka (Budget speech): social media ban for children below 16.
Andhra Pradesh: bar children below 13 within 90 days; considering rules for 13–16.
Economic Survey 2025–26 recommended age-based limits and stronger platform responsibility.
NHRC discussed the issue on March 16, 2026 (press release March 18).
Australia's Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act, 2024 applies from 10 December 2025.
Under it, platforms must take reasonable steps to stop under-16s from holding accounts.
u0309.trap: Karnataka: below 16; Andhra Pradesh: below 13 – don't swap.

mcq.q: Which Indian state announced in its March 2026 Budget speech a ban on social media for children below 16?
mcq.why: On March 6, 2026, Karnataka announced a social media ban for children below 16.

u0310.gist: Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh released 'Defence Forces Vision 2047' on 10 March 2026, a roadmap for a future-ready, integrated, self-reliant military.
facts: Released at South Block, New Delhi; prepared by Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS).
Ministry of Defence declared 2025 the 'Year of Reforms'.
Era of Transition (till 2030): restructuring, deterrence, indigenous drones and surveillance.
Era of Consolidation (2030–2040): cyber and space integration; layered air and missile defence.
Era of Excellence (2040–2047): fully integrated, self-reliant, all-domain force.

mcq.q: Under 'Defence Forces Vision 2047', released in March 2026, what is the 2030–2040 phase called?
mcq.why: The Era of Consolidation (2030–2040) deepens cyber and space integration.

u0311.gist: On 10 March 2026 the Cabinet approved Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0, shifting it from building infrastructure to a service-based drinking water model.
facts: Total outlay ₹8.69 lakh crore; Centre's share ₹3.59 lakh crore (₹1.51 lakh crore extra).
Target: tap connections to all 19.36 crore rural households by December 2028.
About 15.80 crore households (81.61%) have tap water as of March 2026; 3.23 crore (17%) in 2019.
'Sujalam Bharat' digital platform gives each village a unique Sujal village ID.
Gram Panchayats certify 'Har Ghar Jal' only after operation and maintenance is ensured; 'Jal Utsav' yearly.
JJM launched on 15 August 2019, aiming at tap water for every rural household by 2024.
u0311.hook: Centre's share: old 2.08 + extra 1.51 = 3.59 lakh crore.
u0311.trap: Total ₹8.69 lakh crore vs Centre's ₹3.59 lakh crore. 'Jal Arpan' = Panchayat participation; 'Jal Utsav' = annual programme.

mcq.q: Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0, approved in March 2026, by when should all rural households get tap water connections?
mcq.why: Target: tap connections to all 19.36 crore rural households by December 2028.

u0312.gist: The Union Cabinet approved the Regional Connectivity Scheme – Revised (Modified) UDAN on 25 March 2026 for ten years, costing ₹28,840 crore.
facts: Period: FY 2026–27 to 2035–36; funded by Government of India budget support.
Plans 100 airports from existing unserved airstrips; ₹12,159 crore over eight years.
O&M support for three years: up to ₹3.06 crore per airport and ₹0.90 crore per heliport/water aerodrome yearly.
About ₹2,577 crore proposed for around 441 aerodromes.
UDAN launched October 2016 to make flying affordable and link Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
By June 2026: 665 routes, 95 airports/heliports/water aerodromes; 1.64 crore passengers on 3.5 lakh+ flights.
u0312.trap: Title says 'Modified UDAN', text says 'Revised UDAN' – same scheme, ₹28,840 crore, approved 25 March 2026.

mcq.q: Under the Revised UDAN scheme approved in March 2026, how many airports are to be developed from unserved airstrips?
mcq.why: It proposes developing 100 airports from existing unserved airstrips, with ₹12,159 crore.

u0313.gist: India celebrated its 77th Republic Day in 2026 at Kartavya Path with the theme '150 years of Vande Mataram'; two EU leaders were Chief Guests.
facts: Chief Guests: Antonio Costa (European Council President) and Ursula von der Leyen (European Commission President).
30 tableaux: 17 from States/UTs and 13 from Union Ministries.
Sub-themes: 'Swatantrata ka Mantra – Vande Mataram' and 'Samriddhi ka Mantra – Atmanirbhar Bharat'.
Best State tableaux (judges): Maharashtra (Ganeshotsav) first, then Jammu & Kashmir and Kerala.
Best Ministry tableau: Ministry of Culture; Special Prize: Central Public Works Department.
Popular Choice (MyGov poll): Gujarat first, Uttar Pradesh (Culture of Bundelkhand) second, Rajasthan third.
u0313.trap: Judges' best tableau = Maharashtra; Popular Choice best = Gujarat (UP second).

mcq.q: Which state's tableau won first place in the Popular Choice category at Republic Day 2026?
mcq.why: In the MyGov Popular Choice poll, Gujarat was first, followed by Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.

mcq.q: What was the theme of India's 77th Republic Day celebrations in 2026?
mcq.why: The 77th Republic Day was celebrated with the theme '150 years of Vande Mataram'.

u0314.gist: On 29 January 2026 the Supreme Court put the UGC Equity Regulations, 2026 in abeyance, keeping the 2012 regulations in force for now.
facts: Court flagged vagueness, possible misuse and exclusion in the 2026 Regulations.
The Regulations followed SC directions in Abeda Salim Tadvi v. Union of India (2019).
A Bench of Justices Surya Kant and Ujjal Bhuyan had directed UGC to notify enforceable rules.
Caste discrimination defined to cover SCs, STs and OBCs.
Every institution must set up an Equal Opportunity Centre with an Equity Committee headed by the institution head.
Equity Committee meets within 24 hours, reports in 15 working days; head acts within 7 days.
u0314.hook: 24 hours – 15 working days – 7 days: meet, report, act.

mcq.q: Which regulations continue to operate after the Supreme Court kept the UGC Equity Regulations, 2026 in abeyance in January 2026?
mcq.why: The Court directed that the older 2012 UGC Equity Regulations would continue for now.

u0315.gist: NITI Aayog and GIZ India released 'Water Budgeting in Aspirational Blocks', studying water supply and demand in 18 blocks to improve local water security.
facts: Covers 18 Aspirational Blocks in 10 States and a UT, using a digital water-budgeting platform.
Severe deficits: Namchi (94%), Gangiri (60%), Baldeogarh (53%).
Kotri and Abu Road (Rajasthan) over-extract groundwater beyond recharge.
Fatehpur (Bihar) generates runoff but fails to use the stored water well.
Aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

mcq.q: In NITI Aayog's report 'Water Budgeting in Aspirational Blocks', which block was reported with a 94% water deficit?
mcq.why: The report lists Namchi with a 94% water deficit.

u0316.gist: NDA won 202 of 243 seats in the 2025 Bihar Assembly election; Nitish Kumar became CM for the 10th time, then Samrat Chaudhary in 2026.
facts: Polling in two phases: 6 and 11 November 2025 (121 and 122 seats); counting 14 November.
Turnout 67.25%, the highest since 1951; women 71.77%, men 62.73%.
BJP largest party with 89 seats; JD(U) 85; Mahagathbandhan reduced to 35.
RJD won 25 seats but had the highest vote share (23%).
Nitish Kumar sworn in on 20 November 2025 (10th time); resigned on 14 April 2026.
Samrat Chaudhary became Bihar's first BJP Chief Minister on 15 April 2026.

u0316.check: The new CM's surname is spelt both 'Choudhary' and 'Chaudhary' in the text.

mcq.q: Who became the first Chief Minister of Bihar from the BJP, taking oath on 15 April 2026?
mcq.why: Samrat Chaudhary took oath on April 15, 2026 as Bihar's first BJP Chief Minister.

u0317.gist: Kashi Tamil Sangamam 4.0 was held in Varanasi from 2 to 15 December 2025, focusing on Tamil language learning and youth engagement.
facts: Theme: 'Let Us Learn Tamil – Tamil Karkalam'.
Valedictory ceremony on 30 December 2025 with Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan.

KTS 1.0: 2022; KTS 2.0: Dec 2023 at Namo Ghat; KTS 3.0: Feb 2025 on Sage Agastya.

o: Let Us Learn Tamil – Tamil Karkalam

u0318.gist: The Cabinet approved Census 2027 on 12 December 2025 at ₹11,718.24 crore; it will be India's 16th Census and the first by digital means.
facts: Eighth Census since Independence; the last completed Census was in 2011.
Census is a Union subject: Entry 69, Union List, Seventh Schedule; Census Act, 1948.
Phase I Houselisting: 1 April–30 September 2026; Phase II Population Enumeration: February 2027.
Reference date: 00:00 hours, 1 March 2027 (Ladakh and snow-bound areas enumerated September 2026).
Caste enumeration included (CCPA decision, April 30, 2025); 40-question schedule, Question 10 on caste.
Registrar General (under MHA) runs it; Android/iOS apps; about 30 lakh field staff; optional online self-enumeration.
u0318.hook: 16th Census, 8th after Independence; the count 'freezes' at midnight, 1 March 2027.
u0318.trap: Approval date (12 December 2025) is not the reference date (00:00 hours, 1 March 2027). Census 2021 was postponed after COVID-19.

mcq.q: Under which entry of the Union List is the Census a Union subject, as noted for Census 2027?
mcq.why: The Census is a Union subject under Entry 69 of the Union List, Seventh Schedule.

mcq.q: What is the general reference date for Census 2027, approved by the Cabinet in December 2025?
mcq.why: The reference date is generally 00:00 hours on 1 March 2027.

u0319.gist: Round-up of national news: Yoga Day 2026 in Kolkata, Keralam rename approval, PM-RAHAT, BHASHINI, UP's Gharauni Act and the Ayodhya Dharma Dhwaja.
facts: 12th International Yoga Day (21 June 2026): Kolkata, Red Road; theme 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing'; Guinness record.

UP Rural Abadi Records (Gharauni) Act: Governor's assent 2 January 2026; gives legal basis to SVAMITVA property cards.
BHASHINI (BHASHa INterface for India): 36+ text languages, 22+ voice languages, 350+ AI models.
Ayodhya, 25 November 2025: PM hoisted Dharma Dhwaja (10 ft × 20 ft) on Ram Temple Shikhara.
